pairs.note: Rook takes knight; the e6 bishop is pinned on the e-file. Bad twin: a black pawn on e5 blocks the pin.
Queen takes pawn; the f6 knight is pinned on the long diagonal. Bad twin: a white pawn on c3 blocks the pin.
Pinned e6 bishop on both. Bad twin: a black pawn on c6 also attacks d5.
Pinned f6 knight on both. Bad twin: a black rook on e8 also attacks e4.
Rook takes rook (good) or knight (bad); c6 pawn recaptures on both.
Queen takes queen (good) or pawn (bad); e8 rook recaptures on both.
The black pawn is on h5 (off the pin line) in the good twin and on e5 in the bad twin.
The white pawn is on a3 in the good twin and on c3 in the bad twin.

Rook takes knight; the e5 pawn is pinned on the e-file and cannot take on d4. The black rook stands on h3 (14 moves) in the good twin and blocks the pin on e3 (10 moves) in the bad twin, so the enemy has more moves on the good board.
The black pawn is on c7 (attacks d6, not d5) in the good twin and on c6 in the bad twin.
The black rook is on b8 in the good twin and on e8 in the bad twin.
Knight takes pawn; the f6 knight is pinned by the h6 rook and the e6 king attacks d5 on both. The white pawn defends d5 from e4 (good) or stands on a2 (bad).
Rook takes knight; a black pawn on c6 recaptures in the bad twin.
The checker's own test boards: bishop to d6; the e7 bishop is pinned unless a white pawn on e2 blocks the e-file.
The white pawn is on a2 in the good twin and on e2 in the bad twin.
Rook takes rook (good) or knight (bad); the c6 pawn recaptures on both.
Knight to f3; a black pawn on e4 attacks f3 in the bad twin.

bad.note: Rook takes a knight that a pawn recaptures.
